_meta.indication: Add-on maintenance treatment of severe asthma characterized by an eosinophilic phenotype in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter; randomized 2:1 to depemokimab or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and adolescents ≥12 years with eosinophilic asthma (serum eosinophil count ≥300 cells/µL in past year or ≥150 cells/µL at Screening)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annualized rate of clinically significant asthma exacerbations over 52 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Annualized exacerbation rate ratio 0.42 (p < 0.001, 95% CI 0.30, 0.6), a 58% reduction (95% CI 40%, 70%)

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter; randomized 2:1 to depemokimab or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and adolescents ≥12 years with eosinophilic asthma (serum eosinophil count ≥300 cells/µL in past year or ≥150 cells/µL at Screening)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annualized rate of clinically significant asthma exacerbations over 52 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Annualized exacerbation rate ratio 0.52 (p < 0.001, 95% CI 0.36, 0.73), a 48% reduction (95% CI 27%, 64%)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥4%): upper respiratory tract infection (9% vs 8% placebo), allergic rhinitis (6% vs 3%), influenza (5% vs 4%), arthralgia (4% vs 3%), and pharyngitis (4% vs 1%). Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis can occur.
target_moa: IL-5 antagonist; binds soluble IL-5 (dissociation constant 10.5 pM), blocking its binding to the alpha chain of the IL-5 receptor and reducing eosinophils
modality: mAb (humanized, YTE-modified IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; there were no significant or unexpected safety or efficacy issues warranting discussion.

basis.text: Application was reviewed under Standard (not Priority) review.

summary.text: Original BLA 761458 received December 16, 2024 under Standard review, approved December 16, 2025 as a first-cycle approval based on two replicate Phase 3 trials (SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2); no accelerated approval, no advisory committee, with PREA pediatric and pregnancy/lactation postmarketing requirements.

We have approved your BLA for Exdensur (depemokimab-ulaa) effective this date.

requirement.text: 4920-1: Conduct a 52-week, open-label PK, PD, and safety study of depemokimab in pediatric patients 6 to 11 years of age with severe asthma characterized by an eosinophilic phenotype (deferred pediatric study under PREA).

citations.quote: 4920-1Conduct a 52-week, open-label, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and safety study of depemokimab in pediatric patients 6 years to 11 years of age with severe asthma characterized by an eosinophilic phenotype.

requirement.text: 4920-2: Conduct a worldwide descriptive study collecting prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to depemokimab during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications and adverse effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant.

citations.quote: 4920-2      Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to depemokimab during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, and adverse effects on the developing fetus, neonate, and infant.

requirement.text: 4920-3: Perform a lactation study in lactating women who received depemokimab to measure concentrations of depemokimab and its major metabolites in breast milk.

citations.quote: 4920-3      Perform a lactation study (milk-only or mother-infant pair study) in lactating women who have received depemokimab to measure concentrations of depemokimab and its major metabolites in breast milk using a validated assay.
